metadata.title: CBUAE Operational Risk Management Regulation (C 1/2026): Articles 7 and 8, thesis scope
metadata.remarks: Verbatim text retrieved 2026-11-09 from https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/rulebook/operational-risk-management-regulation. Assessment objectives are the thesis criteria.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Only the first half (safeguards for access to and use of assets, including data) is assessed. Early detection and reporting of unauthorized access is a security-monitoring duty and is out of scope.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: As part of the periodic review of processes and control measures, LFIs must identify processes and controls that involve manual interventions and evaluate whether these can be automated, for example through integration into and enforcement by ICT systems. Conversely, for processes and controls that are automated, the effectiveness and accuracy of the automation must form part of periodic assessments and a LFI must identify, measure, monitor and manage the related technology risks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Motivates the engine; not assessed as a criterion.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An LFI must maintain appropriate ICT and cybersecurity infrastructure to meet its current and projected business requirements under normal circumstances and in periods of stress. This infrastructure must ensure data and system integrity, confidentiality and availability and, support integrated and comprehensive risk management.

parts.name: assessment-objective
parts.prose: No flow to a Critical Information Asset during the period uses a cleartext protocol, on any port.

parts.name: assessment-objects
parts.prose: OCSF 4001 Network Activity (flow statistics); config/services.csv

parts.name: guidance

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: At a minimum, the ICT and cybersecurity policy must address the following in support and alignment of the LFI’s business objectives:

parts.name: assessment-objective
